The short answer

Why consults slowed, most important first

  1. Google cut the website's traffic in half in late May. Google's ranking update hit a site that had stood still for two years. About 4 to 5 fewer patients a month now come from Google. It is not the season: last fall your Google visits held steady.
  2. September lost its Fridays. You took most Fridays off. Friday consults fell from 34 in August to 8, which explains most of September's drop on its own.
  3. Social reach collapsed over the summer. TikTok views fell 96% from May to October, and TikTok consults followed about two months later (24 in July and August, 4 in September and October). The videos that worked, explainers and answers to comments, became rare.
  4. You have far fewer reviews than the surgeons around you. 187 Google reviews against 349 for Dr. Talei and about 1,000 for Dr. Desai.
  5. Patients who look you up find Reddit threads about rushed, sales-driven consults. At a higher price, almost everyone checks.
  6. Smaller leaks added up. The booking button was off from August 13. Revision consults are closed online. Every patient must take a concierge call first. Ads cost 51% more per click.

The fix: three moves, plus one idea

Three changes address most of what went wrong. The fourth is an optional idea to bring back your best-performing videos without taking your time. Smaller fixes follow in Part 8.

1 · Reviews

Close the review gap

At least one new Google review every day. Six a day passes Dr. Talei within a month.

2 · Press

Drown out Reddit with indexed press

Articles about you that Google ranks for your name, pushing the Reddit threads down the first page.

3 · Website

Build the new site, then move off Studio 3

A site you own, rebuilt around rhinoplasty, so fixes happen in days instead of years.

4 · Optional idea

Your questions, answered

Did the phone number change?
No. It was decided but never carried out.

Moving everything to the 424 CRM number has been discussed, but it has not happened. As of November 12, the website, your Google profile and your Local AI Registry profile all still show the 323 number, exactly as they did in April. So a number switch did not cause this. But the practice is still split across three numbers, which is its own problem (Part 7).

Did the website change?
No. And that is the problem.

The text on your main Rhinoplasty page has not changed in more than two years. The site has the same pages, layout and settings it had in the spring. Studio 3 updated the gallery pages in August, a dozen core pages in late September, and the homepage description sometime before November 4. None of that touched the pages that win surgery patients. Your Search Console data shows search clicks fell by half starting the week of May 21, when Google released a major ranking update.

Is it just the market?
No. The market explains a little, not half.

Studio 3 points to softer demand and a seasonal dip. Google Trends shows Californians searching for rhinoplasty this fall at the same level as last fall. Last fall your site's Google visits held steady. This year they fell by half in late May and stayed there.

Was it the price increase on July 21?
Not on its own, as far as the data shows.

From July 21 to August 12, each open consult day still held about 4.8 patients, slightly above the 4.65 from January to July. August was one of your best months. The dip came later, alongside the booking button, the Fridays off and the drop in social reach. We cannot see whether consults turned into surgeries at the new price.

Was it the booking button?
Partly, at most.

About a third of consults were booked online before and after August 13, so patients kept finding other ways to book. Patients per open day did slip about 10% after that date. The button is back now, which is right.

Why September?
Mostly the Fridays you took off.

Fridays fell from 34 consults in August to 8 in September, which is 26 of the 32 fewer consults that month. Wednesdays held. October had Fridays again but fewer patients per day, which is where social reach and reputation start to show.

Your booking panel says revision consults are not available. Each step tells a high-value patient to look elsewhere. Part 6

The website and booking

Why Google demoted the site, and where the booking path loses patients.

What a core update does

Why the core update hit sites that stood still

A core update is not a penalty. Google re-ranks the whole web, comparing every page with every other page that could answer the same search. When competitors improve and a site does not, the site loses ground even if nothing on it broke.

Independent analysis of the May 2026 update found that Google rewarded the page that best fit what the searcher wanted, rather than the biggest or oldest site. That hurts a site like this in three ways:

  1. For "rhinoplasty beverly hills," the best fit is a deep, current page about rhinoplasty in Beverly Hills. This site offers a 2024 page of links.
  2. Pages written for one search but aimed at another market, like "best rhinoplasty in Oman," fit no one well.
  3. Off-topic posts make the whole site look less focused on rhinoplasty.

Your data shows that pattern. Your average position barely moved, but the site stopped appearing for about half the searches it used to. Sites typically recover when the next core updates reassess the improved pages, usually several months after the work is done.

  • May 21 to June 2Google rolls out its May 2026 core update. Search clicks to the site fall from about 2,000 a week to about 1,000 a week and stay there.
  • August 6Studio 3 updates the before and after gallery, about 110 gallery pages in one day.

Website audit: what needs to be fixed

We checked every page in the site's sitemap, read the main pages' code and searched Google for how the site's pages compete with each other. The website is where the traffic was lost, so it is where the fix has to start.

The text on your main Rhinoplasty page has not changed in more than two years. We compared the live page word for word with archived copies from October 2024 and September 2025, and only the page title Google shows was edited. The page's own code lists its last update as September 27, 2024. The site's sitemap also lists 59 of its 162 main pages as last updated in September 2024. For a practice that only does rhinoplasty, a stale Rhinoplasty page is a big red flag to Google and to patients.

Cannibalization and semantic search, in plain terms

Cannibalization is when several of your own pages chase the same search. Google will usually rank only one page per site for a search, so your pages split the links, clicks and attention that one page should get. Google often picks the wrong one. On November 12 it showed a short blog post for "bulbous nose" instead of the page that explains Dr. Dugar's procedure.

Semantic search means Google and AI tools no longer match keywords. They work out the topic and judge whether a site covers it completely, clearly and from real expertise. A site that covers rhinoplasty in depth, with every page linking back to one main guide, reads as the authority. A site where rhinoplasty pages sit next to lip plumper recipes and country pages reads as unfocused. ChatGPT and Google's AI Overview make the same judgment when they decide whom to name.

The content the site needs

One rebuilt Rhinoplasty page at the center, with focused pages around it. Each supporting page covers one topic in depth and links back to the center.

What patients find when they look you up

Patients who hear your name search for you before they book. Your Search Console shows about 4,550 appearances for "deepak dugar reviews" and about 4,050 for "deepak dugar rhinoplasty cost." Here is what Google showed them on November 12.

AI summary

Google's AI Overview at the top of "deepak dugar reviews" describes your patient feedback as polarized. It credits Yelp and Healthgrades for praise of your natural results, then cites Reddit for patients who felt rushed in consults or unhappy with results, and for doubts that the closed technique suits complex or revision cases.

Reddit

Reddit

It described you as ideal for a very subtle, undetectable result, but possibly less suited to major structural correction or complex revision. Among the sources it read was the Reddit sales-pitch thread described above. For a premium patient, that story shows up right at the moment they are deciding.

The three big moves and one optional idea in detail, what they cost, the quick fixes, and who owns each.

Effort against impact

1 · Close the review gap

PaceTotal after 30 daysYou pass

  • Ask every patient at the post-op visit, with the QR code in hand
  • Email past patients a direct link to your Google review page
  • Ask everyone, not only the happy ones
  • Never offer anything in exchange
  • Keep a steady daily pace; sudden bursts can be filtered
  • We track the count weekly and report it

2 · Drown out Reddit with indexed press

You cannot delete a Reddit thread, and you should not argue with it. You can give Google better results to show for your name.

  • Feature your Wall Street Journal, People and CBS appearances on the site and Google profile
  • Pitch new stories on closed rhinoplasty, breathing and what a premium consult looks like
  • Each article names you in the headline and links to your website
  • Goal: several press results on page one for "deepak dugar reviews"
  • Turn each article into a short explainer video, so press feeds social
  • Reply once, calmly, from an identified practice account; never use fake accounts
Insight

Press fixes what patients find. The consult experience fixes what they say. Both need work at once, because the Reddit threads, Google’s AI summary and the newest 1-star review all describe the same feeling of being rushed.

3 · Build the new website, then move off Studio 3

Built and maintained by Local AI Registry.

Google demoted the site because it stood still: the main Rhinoplasty page has the same text since September 2024, and dozens of posts are off topic. Moving the site to one the practice owns lets Local AI Registry fix it directly, and frees your main phone number from a vendor's tracking line.

Before anything moves, make sure the practice owns

  • The scarlessnose.com domain and its DNS
  • Admin access to Search Console and Google Analytics
  • Admin access to the Google Ads account
  • Ownership of the Google Business Profile
  • The booking platform account and its widget
  • A main phone number the practice controls (the 424 CRM line)
Phase 1 · Weeks 1 to 2

Secure and plan

Collect every login and admin role above. Map every page that earns clicks. Switch the public number to the 424 line everywhere on the same day.

Phase 2 · Weeks 2 to 6

Build the new site in private

A rebuilt Rhinoplasty guide at the center, with Cost, Consult, Recovery and Traveling Patients pages around it (and Revision, if you reopen it). Phone first, since 83% of visits are on phones. Booking button top right. Instagram and TikTok linked correctly. Off-topic posts retired.

Phase 3 · Launch week

Move without losing rankings

Keep every URL that earns traffic, redirect the merged ones, switch the domain, submit the new sitemap and check Search Console daily for errors.

Phase 4 · Months 2 to 6

Grow

New expert pages every month, reviewed by Dr. Dugar. Sites usually recover when Google's next core updates reassess the improved pages.

Proposed timeline. Decide separately who runs Google Ads after the move.

4 · Optional idea: illustrated explainer videos

Your own TikTok data says what works. In every period, explainers and answers to comments beat patient stories, and answer videos drew about 45,000 views each in the spring. They stopped after June 19, and reach fell with them. You post everything yourself and your time goes to patients, so filming more is not realistic. Illustrated explainers are a way to scale: we turn each patient question into a short animated video, and you only review it.

  • We pull the questions patients ask in your comments and in Google searches
  • We write each answer and tell it with simple animated illustrations
  • You approve every video for accuracy before it goes out
  • We post them on TikTok and Instagram Reels
  • The same answers go on the new website, so videos also help Google and AI
  • Each press feature becomes an explainer too
  • We report views and consults by source every month
Why try it

Patients book about two months after they watch, and 6 in 10 consults name Instagram, TikTok or Facebook. Illustrated explainers are an experiment: we would start with a handful, compare their views with your spring answer videos, and keep going only if they perform. Your own on-camera videos still matter most when you have time for them.
